A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PepCompass and retain matching core methods and experiments. All 25 pages of v4 and 36 pages of v5, including appendices, support comparison through readable text, equations, tables, and rendered figures.

before.justification: V4 reports original computational optimization experiments, decoder-rank analyses, and wet-lab testing of four novel seeds and 25 optimized peptides against 19 bacterial strains.

after.justification: V5 retains these original results and adds optimization, sensitivity, computational profiling, and correlation analyses in its appendices.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–6 retain the same SORBES-SE, MUTANG, local enumeration, LE-BO, and PoGS procedures and objectives. Appendix D develops the previously suggested ambient-metric extensions mathematically; the new explanations and experimental ablation variants do not establish a revision to the retained PepCompass pipeline.

E1.justification: V5 expands beyond antimicrobial-activity optimization to joint hydrophobicity/charge optimization, toxicity minimization, and hydrophobicity maximization (Appendices K and N). The multiobjective experiment uses prototypes from GRAMPA and DRAMP. The wet-lab cohort remains unchanged; the newly detailed prototype controls were already represented in v4's plots.

E2.justification: The external comparator sets in Table 2 and Figure 3 remain unchanged. V5 adds probability-metric PoGS and LE-BO without ROBOT as comparison variants in Tables 3 and 7. SAASBO receives detailed profiling but was already evaluated unsuccessfully within v4's runtime budget; DEEP-AMP and ToxiPep serve as oracles, not competing optimization methods.

E3.justification: New protocols include probability-versus-logit geometry tests, 60-prototype evaluations, multiobjective weights, κ sweeps, additional initialization seeds, and alternative oracle objectives. Appendix M introduces profiling over 10 iterations and six seeds. The retained main experiment still specifies 1,400 evaluations, and the wet-lab procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: V5 substantially extends the existing walk/mutation ablations to test dependence on κ, ROBOT, seed selection, ambient geometry, potentials, and oracles (Appendices K and N). Appendix O examines candidate enumeration and physicochemical properties, while Figure 11 adds a predictor-versus-experimental-activity analysis.

E5.justification: Appendix M newly quantifies runtime variability, including a complete-run duration of 1 h 20 min ± 30 min, and reports runtime/memory dispersion. Appendix O and Figure 11 add Spearman correlation estimation. Table 2 retains mean and standard deviation over 10 runs, and wet-lab measurements retain independent triplicates; no increase in these repetitions is established.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and the original wet-lab summary plots are unchanged. New Tables 3–11 report sensitivity, alternative-objective, oracle, and computational-cost results; Table 5 reports 2.89 ± 2.21 versus 23.31 ± 9.94 seconds per iteration for LE-BO and SAASBO. Table 13 newly supplies peptide-specific MICs, and new figures report geometric and experimental correlations. These are added results rather than gains on the retained benchmark.

T1.justification: Appendix D adds formal mutation and insertion/deletion geometry, mutation-kernel definitions, and a Mahalanobis/transformed-decoder derivation. Appendix H adds a computational-complexity argument. Existing mathematics also changes: Appendix C replaces κ with κ² in its maximality bound, and the Brownian-motion proof revises a Laplacian-comparison factor. The main convergence theorem is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: decoder-derived κ-stable manifolds, geometry-aware global/local search, and successful antimicrobial discovery using four seeds and 25 optimized peptides. V5's explicit abstract statement of 100% validation repeats a claim already present in v4's introduction.

C2.justification: V5 extends the existing length/rank interpretation with a mechanism linking geometry to candidate counts and optimization performance, and links higher rank to lower charge and aromaticity. It develops a biological rationale for the Euclidean ambient metric, discusses kernel-based alternatives, and interprets the new predictor correlation as validating the potential. These substantially expand v4's explanations and limitations discussion.

D1.justification: V5 supplies the previously missing mutation threshold, θmut = 10^-6, and identifies the profiling hardware and memory configuration. Appendix P adds sequence identities, family membership, strain-ID mapping, and peptide-level MIC data for the existing wet-lab study. These materially improve reproducibility; the code-access address and established synthesis/testing instructions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V5 adds references supporting DEEP-AMP, ToxiPep, and the Eisenberg hydrophobicity scale. Appendix A removes the molecule-optimization passage citing 'Mario plays on a manifold.' The broader positioning and novelty claims remain stable; numerous author, year, and venue updates concern already cited works.

P1.justification: The abstract is condensed and reordered, portions of the results discussion are reorganized, and prototype/seed/analog terminology is clarified. The ethics statement expands into an Impact Statement, while the reproducibility and LLM-usage statements are removed. Most retained method exposition and related-work prose remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: V5 redesigns the main text and references into two columns and substantially changes figure, table, and algorithm placement. It adds eleven tables and four figures. Some displays reorganize existing information: Table 12 tabulates previously listed strains, and v4 Figures 8–9 retain their original images as v5 Figures 12–13.

improvement.justification: V5 improves validation and reproducibility through targeted sensitivity/oracle tests, measured computational costs, the missing hyperparameter, and peptide-level sequences/MICs absent from v4. These make the retained headline results easier to scrutinize. The gain is tempered by errors in the added theory: Appendix D.1 equates cosine 1/2 with 30°, and Appendix H's linear-cost argument omits the cost of materializing MUTANG's Cartesian-product candidate set.
